slots.name: file_delete_if_match

slots.name: file_update_atomic_checked
slots.description: R4SYS completes or reverses one SYSUPD ownership transfer only after target, stage and backup fingerprints plus transient filesystem identities match a legitimate journal state under one serialized filesystem gate. The additive long_stage flag permits an existing FAT32 long-name stage for forward completion only; the backup and newly created target remain short names, and the stage short entry is durably detached before its LFN slots are reclaimed.

slots.name: path_names_equal_collated

slots.name: file_update_cleanup_checked
slots.description: R4SYS completes one SYSUPD per-payload cleanup with target, stage, current backup and previous backup bound together to expected identity, size and checksum under one serialized filesystem gate.

slots.name: file_stream_declare_publish
slots.description: R4SYS records the create-only publish intent of an already open stream, including which protocol owns it, so the durable claim brackets the whole transfer instead of only the final hand-over and recovery telemetry can attribute an abandoned stage to SFTP, SCP or FTP.

slots.name: module_resource_stat

slots.name: module_resource_read

slots.name: program_module_path

slots.name: program_module_running

slots.name: storage_inventory

slots.name: storage_device

slots.name: storage_partition
slots.description: Read one partition from the exact complete inventory; invalid or partial tables remain explicit.

slots.name: storage_volume

slots.name: storage_claim_begin
slots.description: Reject stale, partial, protected or used targets before modification; close admissions, drain, flush and unmount, then return an exact logical-thread-owned exclusive claim. Failure returns no claim and performs no raw mutation.

slots.name: storage_claim_end
slots.description: Close raw admission, flush, rescan and remount prior identities unless KEEP_UNMOUNTED is set. A completed close consumes the claim even when I/O or remount fails; BUSY retains a finishing claim for retry. Failed targets remain visible.

slots.name: storage_read
slots.description: Read at most storage_raw_max_sectors from a complete validated target; concurrent exclusive claims return BUSY. The output buffer holds sectors times 512 bytes.

slots.name: storage_claim_read
slots.description: Perform bounded synchronous read within an active caller-owned claim. Buffer remains caller-owned for the call. An I/O error may follow partial hardware progress; never replay writes automatically.

slots.name: storage_claim_write
slots.description: Perform bounded synchronous write within an active caller-owned claim. Buffer remains caller-owned for the call. An I/O error may follow partial hardware progress; never replay writes automatically.

slots.name: storage_claim_flush
slots.description: Issue the durability barrier for an active caller-owned claim and report backend failure.

slots.name: storage_rescan
slots.description: Acquire the complete device, drain/unmount, reread its table and remount matching previous identities. Open uses reject rescan before unmount.

slots.name: storage_mount
slots.description: Probe and mount a complete partition with a fresh generation. Letter zero assigns the first free D through Z except reserved R; C and R cannot be reassigned through this call.

slots.name: storage_unmount
slots.description: Drain and unmount the selected physical volume and its aliases. Required runtime volumes and open uses reject the operation.

slots.name: storage_use_begin
slots.description: Acquire a real physical-volume use lease for a resolved path, including the system boot alias. File and directory handles hold this lease until close or logical owner retirement.

slots.name: storage_use_end
slots.description: Release an exact caller-owned volume use lease; stale or foreign identifiers are rejected.

slots.name: directory_change_begin
slots.description: Capture a directory identity and current change sequence under the filesystem request gate. Returns 0 on success, -1 for invalid cursor/path, -3 for missing mount/directory, -9 for an I/O failure. Register before the initial enumeration.

slots.name: directory_change_poll
slots.description: Consume RAM-only changes for the captured directory. Returns 1 if a reload is needed (also on bounded history overflow), 0 if unchanged, -1 for invalid cursor, -3 for a retired mount. Mutations wake desktop_activity_wait. No persistent allocation and no close.

slots.name: file_copy_buffered
slots.description: Copies under one paired filesystem request, rejecting source aliases before destination mutation. Caller exclusively owns the supplied nonempty buffer until return. File-stream result codes: 0 success, invalid for identical files, too_large above 4 GB, I/O on failure. Progress reports completed appends; failure may leave a partial target. No automatic retry or rollback.

slots.name: notification_create
slots.description: Create a resident process-owned notification with revision zero. Handles never repeat within a boot. Returns notification status; output changes only on success. Allocation failure is explicit. Close explicitly or let exact process retirement reclaim it.

slots.name: notification_query
slots.description: Read the notification revision. Read before testing the userland predicate, then wait with that revision to avoid a lost wake. Foreign or consumed handles are stale; output changes only on success.

slots.name: notification_notify
slots.description: Increment the revision and wake at most wake_count enrolled tasks atomically. Count must be positive; UINT32_MAX broadcasts. A caller racing enrollment observes the changed revision. No permit, CPU-memory ownership or GPU completion is manufactured. Revision exhaustion closes the object and wakes all with closed.

slots.name: notification_wait
slots.description: Wait only while the resident revision equals observed_sequence. Zero polls; UINT64_MAX waits indefinitely. Predicate check, scheduler enrollment and notify share one owner. Returns 0 on change/wake, 1 on timeout, negative on failure/close; caller must recheck its own predicate. Close cancels enrolled waits. Hard kill detaches the actual task node and needs no caller destructor. No caller address or unwind guard is retained across sleep.

slots.name: notification_close
slots.description: Close admission, cancel enrolled waits and release resident backing. Returns 0 after release; retry notification_error_release for the same closed handle. A failed free retains backing and prevents process-slot reuse. Further ordinary operations on a closed retained object fail; a consumed handle is stale.

slots.name: program_local_get
slots.description: Read a process-local immutable publication by nonzero key. Returns program_local_ok and zero if absent. A key can be a boot-stable library token address. Output changes only on success. No other process, user pointer ownership or current-thread identity is exposed.

slots.name: program_local_publish
slots.description: Publish a nonzero process-local value exactly once for a nonzero key. Returns program_local_ok if installed, program_local_existing if another caller already installed a value; both write the winning value. Caller owns candidate memory and discards it when it loses. Published data must outlive all program threads; no replacement, destructor or allocator policy is provided. The process reaper removes metadata after thread retirement and before VM teardown. Errors leave output unchanged.

slots.name: thread_current_handle
slots.description: Copy the calling program thread identity, including thread and process generations, into ProgramJoinHandle. Returns thread_ok on success, thread_error_no_instance outside a program thread, or thread_error_invalid for a null output. Errors leave output unchanged. The identity is borrowed: no pin, join lease, allocation or wait is created; normal status/join admission and retirement rules still apply. Lookup uses the current task execution owner and never scans a registry. Valid for the main thread as well as secondary threads.

slots.name: cpu_capacity
slots.description: Copy current schedulable CPU capacity for ordinary program threads. Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid for null output, or thread_error_busy before capacity is available; errors leave output unchanged. available_cpus counts one atomic scheduler-admission mask snapshot (no process affinity restrictions currently exist). configured_cpus counts dense CPU slots admitted by the boot SMP plan, including failed/offline slots; it is not the CPUID package count, firmware total or kernel maximum. Capacity is advisory, not a reservation, affinity mask, cache topology or performance guarantee. No allocation or wait.

slots.name: program_exit
slots.description: Terminates the entire calling program from its main or a secondary thread. On admission this does not return. reason accepts program_exit_reason_natural or program_exit_reason_failed only; invalid reason returns thread_error_invalid, missing program-thread ownership returns thread_error_no_instance, and a non-sleepable context or held kernel lock/unwind lifetime returns thread_error_busy without initiating exit. The first committed concurrent process exit wins. The existing exit/reaper path closes admission, stops peers and retains stacks, I/O and graphics resources through actual retirement; the caller transfers its own terminal Task to the scheduler reaper. Does not run user destructors, atexit, TLS callbacks, stream flushing or foreign stack unwinding; normal userland shutdown precedes this primitive, fatal shutdown may omit it. External kill still rejects self. Older providers may omit this optional tail.

slots.name: platform_input_snapshot
slots.description: Copy the canonical ACPI/USB Consumer input snapshot without consuming events.1 success, negative invalid output. Caller initializes version1/size64; output unchanged on failure. No hardware access, callback or allocation. Desktop policy observes counter deltas and lid state independently from normal keyboard text.

slots.name: directory_next
slots.description: Resume owner-bound directory enumeration without prefix scans. Initialize DirectoryScanCursor to defaults. Returns 0 file, 1 directory, 2 bounded progress without an entry (retry), -5 complete EOF, -10 restart after directory mutation, history overflow, owner/path/mount change; other negatives are errors (-1 invalid, -3 missing mount, -7 output too small, -9 I/O). On restart/error discard all partial results; no truncated successful generation. Cursor and output are unchanged on errors; progress and EOF publish cursor only. Success copies a NUL-terminated absolute path. One call examines at most 256 physical directory entries, with a bounded NTFS ancestor stack. Internal state is opaque, must not be edited or used concurrently. No persistent kernel resource, allocation or mount pin; discarding/resetting cursor cancels/closes immediately. A call pins its mount and holds the filesystem request gate; an unmount between calls invalidates continuation. Old dir_entry ABI remains unchanged. A found entry also copies FileInfo metadata from the same enumeration record; no second name lookup. NTFS directory-index metadata has the same snapshot semantics as its index entry. On progress, EOF or failure metadata is unchanged.

slots.name: thread_placement_get
slots.description: Get placement of the exact live thread/instance generations (including main). Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid/no_instance/not_found/busy or thread_placement_error_capacity. Validate info version1 and capacity>=64. word_capacity0 allows null cpus and returns metadata including required word count; otherwise capacity must suffice and cpus must be nonnull. Copy exactly cpu_word_count words and64 info bytes on success; all outputs and tails unchanged on errors. Caller buffers must not overlap. No allocation or retained caller pointer.

slots.name: thread_placement_set
slots.description: Set placement of an exact live thread/instance generation (including main). Returns thread_ok, thread_error_invalid/no_instance/not_found/busy/unsupported or thread_placement_error_capacity. Reject unknown flags/class/reserved data, empty sets, unavailable or module-disallowed CPUs and hints outside the set, without state changes. Explicit input length must equal the discovered required word count; default-cpus requires word_count0. Running acceptance may remain pending until full outgoing RSP/FPU save; query revisions. No synchronous wait or realtime guarantee. Repeated equal requests do not renew preferred-class budgets; class toggles share one bounded activation budget. No retained caller pointer.

slots.name: system_power_transition
slots.description: Explicit bounded blocking orderly system transition: power_transition_action_halt/reboot/poweroff. Closes new CPU control ownership and pins current CPU membership before cooperative POWERSVC stop and real same-CPU request return. No Runtime owner over waits. Refusal returns a negative power_transition_error_* and retains real resources without stopping APs; CPU ownership reopens. Accepted transition becomes terminal and does not return. Missing/disabled provider stays functional. Existing nonblocking raw system_halt/reboot/poweroff slots retain their signatures/meanings; with held requests they refuse immediately rather than waiting or falsely acknowledging return. Profiles/parameter policy stay external. timeout_ticks is an explicit wait budget, clamped to5 seconds;0 requests only a bounded poll. Timeout/refusal may follow an already requested cooperative service stop; query status rather than automatic retry. The immediate legacy slots never perform this new service wait.

slots.name: entropy_source_info
slots.description: Purely cached registered-device source observation. Original source/driver epoch and module generation retained after close. No callback/device/CPU instruction, I/O or entropy consumption.

slots.name: entropy_fill
slots.description: Explicit bounded registered-device source read,1..4096bytes. Ordinary task with IF on, exact task admission through output, exact driver instance/lifecycle lease through resident callback/staging, no Runtime owner over wait. Release driver owner before potentially paged caller copy. Positive exact count only with confirmed full receipt; failure discards/clears valid caller range, never initial/partial entropy. No RNG pool or clock/ID substitute; SDK owns RDRAND-first/source choice.

slots.name: program_lifecycle_begin
slots.description: Nonblocking process-registry epoch admission only. Initializes the existing cursor with initialized|lifecycle, snapshot_generation=program_epoch, no registry traversal, allocation, VM, heap, task or thread diagnostics. Failure leaves cursor unchanged; Busy is not lifecycle authority. Does not cache or equate program epochs with all mutable metadata.

slots.name: program_lifecycle_programs
slots.description: One bounded generation-ordered lifecycle page from the canonical process registry, including pending/done completions. Forty-byte records carry exact handles and current process fields without VM statistics. Epoch mismatch returns restart with no row/cursor advancement; Busy/invalid has no complete authority. Complete paging must finish before adoption/disappearance decisions; revalidate exact handles at actions. A lifecycle cursor cannot be used by full inventory calls or vice versa.

slots.name: drive_info_geometry
slots.description: Returns the same mounted drive identity/capacity and scalar cluster geometry without executing FREE or reading a free-space bitmap. Existing exact mount/request admission can wait. Free fields and drive_info_flag_free_valid are zero: explicitly unknown, not measured zero. Existing DriveInfo56 layout unchanged. index0..25; returns1 mounted,0 unmounted,-1 invalid index,-2 request unavailable.

slots.name: directory_batch
slots.description: Initialize with path and default2160-byte cursor; continuation uses its captured node/path with exact logical-owner, mount and mutation validation. Return1..capacity complete1120-byte records,0 bounded progress,-5 EOF; -1 invalid,-3 absent/not-directory initially,-7 full-path bounds,-9 I/O/admission,-10 stale/foreign/cancel. Capacity1..8; one shared256-step backend budget and prepared metadata per visit. Initialized capacity0/out=NULL validates without advancing (RAM-only while namespace unchanged); input path is ignored on continuation. No persistent kernel allocation/scan lease; call guards always release, including caller unwind. Outputs/cursor have no authority on error. A caller must not modify or concurrently reuse a cursor.

slots.name: program_observation_retain
slots.description: Create an independent observation binding to the exact process handle and generation while its completion record still exists. slots.name: gui_frame_begin_replace

slots.name: gui_frame_stream_info

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_create

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_destroy

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_map_write
slots.description: Reserves one currently unreferenced backing buffer and returns its direct producer-writable address and an unforgeable write token. The mapping becomes immutable when published.

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_publish

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_acquire

slots.name: gui_shared_raster_release

slots.name: gfx_buffer_describe

slots.name: gfx_buffer_import
slots.description: Imports a live shareable reference into the current caller, preserving immutable mode. Producer exit closes new imports; existing references survive.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_release
slots.description: Drops one caller reference; maps, device jobs and scanout retain their own leases. Stale or duplicate release has no effect.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_map
slots.description: Retains a CPU read (0) or write (1) map with an explicit 64-bit range. Conflicting consumers return Busy; WC reads and unavailable CPU mappings are unsupported.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_unmap

slots.name: gfx_buffer_export_raster
slots.description: Exports an exact held shared-raster consumer lease as an immutable BO reference without a pixel copy. The producer may not overwrite the buffer while that reference survives.

slots.name: gfx_buffer_stats

slots.name: gfx_queue_open
slots.description: Opens one bounded asynchronous queue for the current program. Unknown adapters or milestones return unsupported; no silent fallback.

slots.name: gfx_queue_close
slots.description: Closes the caller queue, cancels every pending fence, and drops caller fence references. Physical device uses survive until acknowledged quiescent.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit
slots.description: Returns after acceptance without executing commands or copying pixels. All descriptors and up to eight dependencies are copied; source/target leases retain backing and prevent premature CPU reuse. Failure leaves output and existing latest-frame work untouched.

slots.name: gfx_fence_query
slots.description: Snapshots one exact fence without waiting. A terminal cancellation may still report device-active; resources are reusable only after physical quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_fence_wait
slots.description: Waits without spinning or holding a metadata owner. timeout_ticks is a scheduler-tick duration, with UINT64_MAX meaning indefinite; the submission deadline remains independently finite in monotonic nanoseconds. Wait timeout leaves output unchanged and does not cancel the job. wait_for=0 waits for logical completion; wait_for=1 waits until the operation is physically quiescent and every queue BO lease has been released. Both events are sticky and generation-retained.

slots.name: gfx_fence_cancel
slots.description: Requests the sole logical cancelled completion for a caller-owned fence. Already terminal returns already-completed. Never asserts native DMA quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_fence_release
slots.description: Drops the caller fence reference. Active backing, dependency edges, wake publication and task-generation waiter records prohibit premature slot reuse.

slots.name: gfx_queue_backend
slots.description: Queries one fixed backend inventory slot, from zero through gfx_queue_backend_capacity minus one. Zero is software; other slots may be vacant. Returns 1 with an exact binding, 0 for vacant, negative for error; output changes only on 1. Revalidate by opening with the returned generations. No hidden fallback or successful partial enumeration.

slots.name: gfx_output_revision
slots.description: Reads the output revision used with existing desktop activity waits. No second event queue and no busy polling are required.

slots.name: gfx_output_info
slots.description: Reads one of the advertised fixed catalog slots; holes return zero without modifying output. Stable ports survive disconnects, receiver generations do not.

slots.name: gfx_output_mode
slots.description: Reads one source-filtered mode for an exact receiver incarnation. Stale never returns data belonging to a different receiver.

slots.name: gfx_output_edid
slots.description: Copies one complete raw EDID block for an exact receiver incarnation. Missing blocks return zero; invalid/stale leaves output unchanged.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_test
slots.description: Checks the complete output/geometry/format/pitch/PLL/plane/bandwidth/fence state without reservations or device writes. Native commits remain unsupported until hardware and all desktop consumers negotiate the full pipeline.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_commit
slots.description: Revalidates the complete state before committing. Currently the firmware backend only supports retaining its actual fixed scanout. Unnegotiated native mode/puffer changes return unsupported before any hardware write. Commit outcomes never imply VBlank.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_submit
slots.description: Submit an asynchronous single-primary native atomic change. Copies the complete state and retains full source references before returning. Requires an opted-in native backend and a 1000..60000 ms confirmation interval. Returns queued status, never a hardware success. Unsupported geometry or unavailable capability has no device effects.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_status
slots.description: Read the retained mode transaction without waiting. Ticket zero reads the latest transaction for diagnostics; an explicit obsolete ticket returns stale. Reading is allowed across caller exit and hardware loss.

slots.name: gfx_atomic_resolve
slots.description: The submitting program confirms the visible candidate or requests rollback. Confirmation is accepted only before its deadline. Cancellation and timeout are requests for actual driver rollback; backing remains retained until real completion. Status is nonblocking; caller exit does not stop the deadline worker.

slots.name: display_presentation_stats
slots.description: Read coherent per-head statistics from the current native primary backend. Returns gfx_output_ok or a negative gfx_output error, with no output mutation on failure. No waits, device calls or CPU-copy fence reinterpretation. Unsupported/boot framebuffer backends have no visible hardware completion sample.

slots.name: display_cursor_submit
slots.description: Submit one finite asynchronous cursor operation for the calling program. Busy keeps prior state. Prepare borrows the source until terminal completion; only successful show/hide confirmation changes visible ownership.

slots.name: display_cursor_status
slots.description: Read coherent primary cursor status without rendering or waits. A caller must not draw software while hardware visibility is confirmed or unknown.

slots.name: gfx_queue_backend_info

slots.name: gfx_native_start
slots.description: Start a caller-owned native BO allocation. Copies input and returns a pending request. Exact provider memory generation and finite deadline required; at most 16 requests per program. No R4D callback executes on the application task. Receive or close each successful request; error leaves output unchanged.

slots.name: gfx_native_query
slots.description: Inspect a request owned by the current program. Logical terminal status does not prove physical driver cleanup. Output changes only on success.

slots.name: gfx_native_receive
slots.description: Atomically transfer a successful request-held BO reference to the current program and consume the request. Pending reports busy, failed returns its recorded error. Capacity failure leaves request available for retry. Output changes only on success.

slots.name: gfx_native_close
slots.description: Close a caller-owned allocation request; discard unreceived result and cancel queued work. Claimed work, provider callback and enrolled waiters remain retained until their exact completion. Cannot imply GPU or firmware quiescence.

slots.name: gfx_native_wait
slots.description: Wait on sticky request completion outside owner locks. Exact task-generation wait record survives hard task termination until reaper detach. Relative wait timeout leaves the request and output unchanged; allocation deadline separately closes logical work. Returns terminal status on 1, including failed/cancelled result.

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_render_list

slots.name: display_presentation_info

slots.name: display_presentation_feedback

slots.name: gfx_queue_submit_output

slots.name: display_output_presentation_feedback

slots.name: gfx_virtual_query

slots.name: gfx_brightness_request

slots.name: font_prefix_metrics2

Returns0 complete with unique nonzero bank revision/count/complete flag; -7 capacity reports required_count with no usable rows; all other errors grant no output authority. Empty source/capacity0 is a constant-work checked font stamp probe, no full text scan. Caller keeps immutable source and whole aligned disjoint exclusive outputs/code through real synchronous return. No heap, global text cache, persistent handle, second font owner, rendering/shaping/kerning or current-font/physical completion promise. Canonical font revision wrap permanently refuses new metrics rather than reusing identities; existing font APIs remain unchanged.

slots.name: memory_kernel_heap_check

Exclusive with native boot probes. No global reserve-failure injection, timer reprogramming or artificial clock advancement; those isolated cases are advertised separately. Returns 1 for a fixed report, 0 when unavailable, -1 for invalid selection/header/capacity without output mutation. Failed cleanup retains the resident session and prevents new work; never retry automatically.

Returns 1 for a fixed report including busy/failure/cancellation, 0 when context unavailable, -1 for invalid header/capacity unchanged output.
